newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid agencies ready to enter rebel-held Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Aid agencies ready to enter rebel-held Zaire.

text.p: Aid agencies were preparing to enter Tutsi rebel-held eastern Zaire to assess the needs of more than a million starving Hutu refugees trapped by ethnic fighting after rebel leaders agreed to open relief corridors for them.
Omar Backhet, of the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), told Reuters the first assessement teams would enter the eastern Zaire rebel-held cities of Bukavu and Goma early on Monday.

"We have reached an agreement with them (rebels) and we'll be sending in assessement teams first thing tomorrow. The teams will be made up of non-governmental agencies and within a day or two U.N. agencies should be able to go in as well," Backhet said.
He was speaking after U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien returned to Rwanda for further talks on the situation in eastern Zaire.

Chretien told a news conference he would hold talks with President Pasteur Bizimungu and military strongman Major-General Paul Kagame on how to end fighting and to deploy a U.N. humanitarian force in the area.

The U.N. enovy told reporters in Kigali, where he arrived from the Ugandan capital Kampala, that his second visit to Rwanda within two days was aimed at trying to narrow wide-ranging differences between Zaire and Rwanda.
Zaire accuses Rwanda of backing the rebellion in eastern Zaire. Kigali denies the accusations, saying the war, triggered by Zairean attempts to expel ethnic Tutsis to Rwanda, was an internal matter.

Chretien said he would be also be seeking to underpin a three-week ceasefire in eastern Zaire announced unilaterally by the rebels last week, which has been disrupted by sporadic fighting around Goma and near Bukavu airport.
European Union humanitarian commissioner Emma Bonino was expected in Kigali early on Monday to add her voice to calls for a humanitarian corridor.
Bonino will be arriving from Kinshasa where the government has ruled out safe havens for thousands of refugees who first arrived in 1994 after fleeing ethnic war and genocidal killings in Rwanda.
